item.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh
item.description: Following India's historic success in the recent Operation Sindoor, this budget has reaffirmed the Central government's resolve to further strengthen the country's defence system... This budget lives up to the sentiments and expectations of the people, and gives a solid foundation to the PM's vision of an 'Aatmanirbhar Viksit' Bharat 2047, in which detailed arrangements have been made for the development of all sectors of society. Image:

item.title: Road Transport & Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari
item.description: These initiatives reflect a vision that infrastructure is an enabler of resilience, opportunity, and global competitiveness... New announcements place infrastructure at the centre of India's journey towards the resolution of a 'Viksit Bharat' (Developed India) by 2047. Budget 2026 places infrastructure at the heart of India's journey towards Viksit Bharat 2047. Image:

item.title: Fiscal Deficit
item.description: Budget 2026 pegs fiscal deficit at 4.3% of GDP in FY27, 10 basis points below the estimated 4.4 per cent in in FY26.

item.title: Record Capex
item.description: FY27's capital expenditure is pegged at an unprecedented Rs 12.2 lakh crore, up 8.8% over the previous year.

item.title: LTCG & STCG on buybacks
item.description: Share buybacks will attract capital gains taxes based on the holding period.

item.title: Higher F&O STT
item.description: Derivatives trades (futures and options) will attract higher securities transaction tax.

item.title: Easier PROI Rules
item.description: Budget has doubled an investment limit applicable to persons resident outside India to 10%.
